correctness.rationale: The exact small-divisor pairing gives |S′(n)|=(tau(n)-2)/2 for nonsquares and (tau(n)-1)/2 for squares; the square threshold is correctly excluded as O(sqrt X). For nonsquare least-prime-p integers, tau(n)<=2(p+1) bounds the number of other distinct prime factors by u=floor log2(p+1). Patterns with u distinct first-power primes contribute via Landau, and the allowed exponent of p satisfies (e+1)2^u<=2(p+1), i.e. e<=E. Every other finite exponent pattern has fewer free first-power primes; summable prime-square weights and Landau show negligible total. Exhaustive independent divisor-set and divisor-count checks succeeded for n=2..250000, including every perfect square; they do not replace Landau or the infinite argument.

value.rationale: The paper motivating the question proves vanishing density, but this does not tell how numerous Schreier integers are inside each fixed least-prime stratum. The theorem gives a complete asymptotic hierarchy with explicit constants, shows phase transitions when the permissible number of other prime factors increases, and identifies exactly when a second p-power layer changes the leading constant (for p=2 from 1/2 to 3/4). These are natural quantitative data directly tied to the small-divisor Schreier condition; the result does not claim a globally summed asymptotic or paper-scale consequence.
